Articulation Agreement Overview

This agreement outlines lower-division course requirements specific to the major. Students are strongly encouraged to consult an academic advisor to ensure they meet all degree requirements for their intended baccalaureate program.


Helpful Resources:

  • CSUB Catalog
  • Transfer Admission Requirements
  • Academic Advising Student Centers
  • CSUB Program Pathways Mapper


Course Equivalency Information for 4-Year Institutions

Students and staff can explore course transfer equivalencies through the Transfer Evaluation System (TES). Equivalency agreements are updated regularly and subject to change. For the most current information, please refer to TES or contact the Articulation Office.

","groupId":"91bbdb0a-2e7f-4d88-853a-019e1e332eec","position":1,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"About the Major","groupId":"ec98f517-aeec-4854-ae19-019e1e332eec","position":2,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"

The Bachelor of Arts degree in Child, Adolescent, and Family Studies (CAFS) at California State University, Bakersfield provides breadth and depth in the scientific study of the child, adolescent, and adult developmental domains. The program focuses on the biological, cognitive, psychological, and sociological foundations of learning from early childhood development, through adolescent growth, and adult behavior. The program design is based on contemporary learning theories, the application of ethics and values, research methods, and diverse family systems/approaches, with practical applications in disciplines that require direct interaction with children and families.


For additional information, visit the following:

Department of Child Adolescent, and Family Studies

Program Requirements - Child, Adolescent, and Family Studies, BA
